item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Haung: ‘We have to accelerate AI safety’
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Haung: ‘We have to accelerate AI safety’
2026-10-22
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-we-have-to-accelerate-ai-safety-124206653.html
Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang says the AI industry needs to focus on safety following this summer's revelations that AI agents from leading labs broke free of containment and hacked into websites, including Hugging Face.
"It shouldn't have happened. Doesn't need to happen," Huang told Deirdre Bosa at Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference.
During his keynote on Wednesday, Huang revealed Nvidia's OpenShell Reference Architecture, which the company said will allow customers to build, contain, and observe AI agents. If an agent attempts to go rogue, Nvidia said the system can intervene and stop it.
"Hugging Face developed an exercise, a simulator, and they came to the conclusion: If OpenShell existed, their website wouldn't have been attacked that way," Huang said.
"We have to accelerate AI safety, and safety technology and capability to me is one and the same … As much as it is capable, you want it to be safe. The two of them are really one and the same. And so in the future, as we develop these AI capabilities, safety will come along with it," he added.
Part of that effort, the CEO said, comes down to establishing a zero-trust system around AI agents. Zero trust is a framework for protecting connected systems by limiting their exposure to other platforms and requiring people and platforms to regularly verify their identities.
Doing so, the thinking goes, reduces exposure to hacking and other cyberattacks.
"These agents are autonomous systems, and when you have an autonomous system on your computer … you should first start with zero trust, and give it minimum privileges, minimum access, minimum use of tools," Huang explained.
"Maybe they could access a file, but they can't delete the file. Maybe they can access the internet, but they can't … send stuff out," he added. "And so there are a lot of different things you could specify. Those practices about how to deploy agents and deploy autonomous systems [have] to be adopted across the board right away."
According to Huang, Nvidia is working with more than 100 companies to develop features to manage AI agents using OpenShell.
"We're working with all the labs and working with all the operating system companies. I think the [hacking incidents were] unfortunate, but I think that it's very much transformative for the industry," he added.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says data center builders have to be ‘good neighbors’
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says data center builders have to be ‘good neighbors’
2026-10-22
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-says-data-center-builders-have-to-be-good-neighbors-132705446.html
Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang says that for data center builders to win over communities, they must first partner with them and be good neighbors.
"When you go into a community … before you start building, you ought to extend yourself out to the local community and partner with them," Huang told Deirdre Bosa during the company's GTC event in Berlin.
"Let them know what you're about to do is going to bring, of course, all the benefits, but it's going to, of course, bring new neighbors," he said.
Data center construction has faced major pushback across the US, with some counties and towns instituting outright bans on the facilities. New York has placed a one-year, statewide moratorium on data center construction. Texas, meanwhile, has put connecting new data centers to its grid on hold as it works to determine their potential impact.
The issue has even become a flash point in the midterm elections, with President Trump backing data center development, and Democrats and some Republicans campaigning against them.
Residents have lodged complaints about the constant noise generated by data centers, water usage, increased electricity costs, and more.
To help ease tensions with local residents, some companies, including Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN), have taken steps to win over municipalities by dropping controversial nondisclosure agreements (NDAs).
NDAs have become a key issue among some data center opponents, as they prevent local leaders from disclosing information about the projects.
"Everybody has now taken a step back, whether it's the NDAs or contributing to the communities, whether it's building shops and … community centers and improving schools and in many cases even supporting lower taxes and, you know, all kinds of benefits that can be brought to the local communities," Huang said.
"I think those are all good ideas, and each one of them ought to be … tailored for the needs of the community. But the most important thing is you've got to be a good visitor. You know you should be a good guest. And before you go into a community, stop by and see if you can be helpful," he added.

item.title: Where people make over $1 million a year but still choose to rent
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Where people make over $1 million a year but still choose to rent
2026-10-22
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/where-people-make-over-1-million-a-year-but-still-choose-to-rent-100000195.html
For even America's highest earners, renting can look more appealing than buying a home.
The number of renters in the US earning $1 million and up more than tripled between 2020 and 2024, according to RentCafe data, outpacing the growth in high-earning homeowners during the same period.
The data suggests that even the country's highest earners, while likely able to afford to buy if they wanted to, aren't immune to trends that have pushed millions of Americans to rent for longer. High mortgage rates still curtail their buying power, strong stock market performance makes tying up money in a home look less appealing, and renting can be a more flexible option than going through the process of buying and selling a high-end home.
Most $1 million-earning renter households are concentrated in the nation's priciest cities, where salaries tend to be higher and the cost differential between renting and owning often aggressively favors renting.
In New York City, home to more than 7,000 of these high-earning renters, a monthly rent of $15,000 to $20,000 — considered "comfortable" on that income by conventional affordability metrics — can cover a two- or three-bedroom apartment overlooking Central Park or a two-story unit in the trendy West Village. Buying a comparable unit, though, usually costs far more after factoring in high mortgage rates, taxes, and monthly maintenance fees.
San Francisco has the second-highest population of high-earning renters, with more than 1,800, followed by Los Angeles with 1,500.
But high-earning renters are increasingly popping up in small and midsize cities. Harrisburg, Pa., the state's capital, now has more than 140 renter households making over $1 million, up from just three in 2020. In Provo, Utah, the figure jumped from 10 to 264 in four years. Des Moines, Iowa, saw its highest-earning renters increase from four to 92 during the same period.
Most high-earning renters work in well-paying industries such as technology and finance or hold executive or managerial roles within their companies. About three-quarters of renter households bring in more than $1 million a year by combining two relatively high salaries, rather than having a single person rake in seven figures.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Buffett’s Berkshire just trounced chip stocks and flashed a rare dot-com-era signal
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Buffett’s Berkshire just trounced chip stocks and flashed a rare dot-com-era signal
2026-10-22
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/buffetts-berkshire-just-trounced-chip-stocks-and-flashed-a-rare-dot-com-era-signal-165123739.html
For three weeks, Wall Street sold the hottest trade in the market and bought one of the oldest. Chip stocks lost 15% while Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway gained 7%.
That swing carried Berkshire's Class B stock (BRK-B) to a record close Tuesday, its first since May 2, 2025 — the day before Buffett said he would hand the CEO job to Greg Abel. The stock pushed to an intraday record Wednesday, as did the Class A stock (BRK-A).
The wait took 17 months, a stretch in which the S&P 500 (^GSPC) gained more than 35%.
From Oct. 6 through Tuesday, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell in 10 of 11 sessions. Berkshire rose on nine of those days, and on chips' two worst days, Oct. 14 and Oct. 16, it posted two of its best gains of the run.
For now, that price action has made Berkshire look like a hedge against the AI chip trade. Since Oct. 1, it has mostly risen on the days chips fell.
Berkshire is on track to rise in 14 of its last 15 sessions. Along the way, it strung together a 10-day winning streak, its first since 2018, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
A gap last seen during the dot-com bust
From Oct. 2 through Tuesday, Berkshire beat SOXX by 22 percentage points. That's the widest gap over any 12-session stretch since early 2010, according to Yahoo Finance calculations that compare Berkshire with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) back to 1994. The 12-session window is the one that captures this month's widest gap.
The rarer signal is the combination.
Chips fell at least 14% while Berkshire gained at least 7% over 12 sessions. Before this month, that last happened Oct. 3, 2001. Every earlier case came in 1995-96 or in 2000-01, the latter as the dot-com bubble burst.
History sends a mixed message from here.
In the near term, chips bounced. They were higher a week later in five of the six earlier cases, and they're rebounding Wednesday,too. A year out, chips were lower in five of six instances, and the S&P 500 fell in four.
Four of those six cases came during the same bear market, though. Treat this as a rare signal, not a forecast.
Abel's Berkshire is spending again
Abel has also changed how Berkshire uses its cash. Berkshire bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the second quarter and ended 14 straight quarters of net stock selling while its cash pile fell from a record $397 billion.
Buffett said Sept. 18 he would also step down as chairman. The stock bottomed two weeks later.
The next test comes with third quarter results, expected to be released Saturday, Nov. 7.

item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
2026-10-22
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-reveals-plans-for-an-ai-factory-in-a-shipping-container-to-build-data-centers-in-weeks-not-months-125029004.html
Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
Nvidia (NVDA) wants to reduce the time it takes for its customers to start generating revenue from its AI systems.
At its GTC event in Berlin on Wednesday, the company unveiled its DSX POD, a reference design for an AI data center packed into a box about the size of a standard shipping container.
Data center construction can take months, if not years, to get up and running. And because they don't start generating revenue until they begin processing AI tokens, the longer a data center takes to come online, the more expenses pile up.
The DSX POD is meant to serve as a faster, modular solution for companies that need access to data center capabilities sooner rather than later.
"The moment then you have to install these AI factories, and they're gigantic. And putting these AI factories into service takes months. If we could reduce that months, you know, from the moment that the systems are shipped to the moment that it's deployed and being operational, if we could reduce it from months to weeks or even a month, that will be completely game-changing for all of these AI factories," CEO Jensen Huang told Deirdre Bosa.
According to Nvidia, the Vera Rubin-powered DSX PODs will arrive on site, ready to be plugged into the power, cooling, and networking infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to 14 days.
The company said DSX PODs won't replace traditional data centers, but will serve as a means to start running AI applications before brick-and-mortar facilities are ready.
"With Nvidia DSX POD, we're bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.
According to the company, the DSX POD supports liquid cooling, but because it uses dry-cooler designs, it can save up to 54 million liters of water per day versus a standard data center.
Standing up data centers more quickly doesn't just help Nvidia's customers, though. Faster data center deployment should ease at least one of the chokepoints in the AI build-out, which means faster chip sales for Nvidia.
Semiconductors aren't the only bottleneck for data center builders. Getting the electricity necessary to power those processors is also a concern. And power plants take far longer to construct than data centers.
Nvidia said it's working with partners, including Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, Dell Technologies (DELL), Foxconn, and others, to begin delivering the DSX POD in early 2027.

item.title: The simple reason JPMorgan thinks SpaceX will triple: It's going after a $28 trillion market
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
The simple reason JPMorgan thinks SpaceX will triple: It's going after a $28 trillion market
2026-10-22
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-simple-reason-jpmorgan-thinks-spacex-will-triple-its-going-after-a-28-trillion-market-183620489.html
SpaceX (SPCX) is on a roll. After reporting earnings for the second time as a public company — turning a profit and showing massive AI revenue — investors are pouring in, driving a 10% gain on Wednesday and stock upgrades from Wall Street.
One analyst note stood out among a strong field: JPMorgan's massive bull thesis. It's common enough for CEO Elon Musk to bet big on himself. But analyst Doug Anmuth laid out another optimistic case, more than doubling his price target to $500 from $240, implying an upside of more than 200% from Wednesday's price.
The reason? In a sentence: "No other company is as well positioned to go after the combined anticipated [total addressable market] of $28T+," Anmuth wrote in a note after earnings.
In other words, SpaceX is going after everything.
Musk's (current) favorite corporate child has already gone beyond rockets and satellites into telecommunications and a complete chip to data center to Grok vertical integration AI, which has overtaken the rest of SpaceX's operations to become its biggest business by revenue. Alone, these businesses would be huge. Together, they approach a quarter of US GDP.
Just imagine if robotaxi and robotics markets get tacked on to that.
In the corporate world, focus often means success — finding the right product, targeting the right customers, and defining the specific value your firm brings. But when you're a giant tech conglomerate, your lane extends to market conquest. Everything is up for grabs, and the name of the game is planting flags. The space race, the AI race, and even, for Musk, the telecom race and supplanting legacy carriers like AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS).
All of this makes the Tesla (TSLA) angle especially interesting. If SpaceX is already on its way to the moon, why not merge with an EV, robotics, and robotaxi company too? The boards of both companies have formed special committees to explore a tie-up. Yet another reason why Musk's enormous ambitions and SpaceX's promising start as a publicly traded company can prompt such lofty projections.
On the company's earnings call Tuesday, Musk said he projects SpaceX's annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 to fall "somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion." This quarter gave us a hint of where things are going, revealing how, in the span of a few months, SpaceX morphed into a new, AI-forward company. The current quarter and the year ahead might very well show another astonishing leap.
Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban.

item.title: Tesla stock slips despite Q3 earnings beat, better-than-expected capex spend
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
Tesla stock slips despite Q3 earnings beat, better-than-expected capex spend
2026-10-22
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/tesla-stock-slips-despite-q3-earnings-beat-better-than-expected-capex-spend-101521707.html
Tesla (TSLA) reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings, with its free cash flow and capex spending coming in ahead of Wall Street estimates.
Tesla reported Q3 revenue of $28.05 billion vs. Bloomberg consensus of $28.13 billion. Tesla posted adjusted EPS of $0.48 vs. the $0.44 estimate, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.90 billion vs. $3.66 billion.
Tesla stock fell almost 5% before the bell on Thursday, with Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein claiming the market was reacting to "capacity constraints in the company's auto and battery growth, which could slow near-term growth."
But that might not be the whole story. Tesla reported free cash flow of $1.53 billion vs. an estimated -$4.92 billion, with capital expenditures climbing to $4.732 billion vs. an estimated $7.96 billion for the quarter.
On the earnings call, Tesla updated its full-year capex guidance to $20 billion from $25 billion previously. Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the savings would come from "managing our capital deployment efficiently, and plan to fund [capex] primarily from our cash flows from operations," he said.
"I think capex is actually ending up being a little lower than we anticipated, but we'll start to become more meaningful next year. And then noticeable in the tens of billions in '28," CEO Elon Musk said on the call.
Roundhill CEO Dave Mazza posits the cutting capex means the Tesla isn't transitioning fast enough to an AI-focused company betting on robotaxis, Optimus robots, and compute.
Tesla revealed its Optimus robot started production at its Fremont factory. "While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product," the company said in its earnings release.
"I would expect that it takes us probably at least a year — maybe a little longer — to get to that annualized rate [1 million units], to get to 20,000 units a week," Musk said on the earnings call. Musk added that Tesla may release an Optimus demo video in about a month, stressing that he didn't want the robot's movements to be preplanned.
Regarding its other AI efforts, Tesla said it plans to reach 400 MW of AI training compute by the end of the year. Tesla said its active FSD (full self-driving) subscriptions climbed to 1.74 million.
"The biggest driver of demand is full self-driving," Musk said regarding vehicle sales.
"The Cybercab fleet in Austin has grown by a factor of 10," Musk added while discussing Tesla's robotaxi fleet. He added, "I don't think there's any company in the world that can match our scale with autonomous vehicles."
Musk also stirred the pot recently with comments about a possible tie-up with SpaceX, his other company.
"I think both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea," Musk said during SpaceX's earnings call Tuesday night. "At the request of shareholders, and these special committees consist of independent directors. And because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees."
He added, "I don't think we should necessarily assume that I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty. And I think that would be overstating it. Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes."
On the Tesla call, Musk briefly touched on it but added nothing new. "With regard to a potential merger with SpaceX, I think I said everything that should be said yesterday [Tuesday]," Musk said.
Teslareported Q3 deliveries of 486,532, down 2% from a year ago but well ahead of the Bloomberg consensus of 463,000. Energy storage deployments came in at 13.7 GWh, up from 12.5 GWh a year ago and Q2's 13.5 GWh.
Tesl

item.title: US to Tap National Diesel Reserve as Prices Soar Before Election
item.author: Ari Natter
item.description:
US to Tap National Diesel Reserve as Prices Soar Before Election
2026-10-22
Por Ari Natter
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/us-tap-national-diesel-prices-132130934.html
(Bloomberg) -- The Trump administration is tapping an emergency reserve of diesel set aside to heat homes in the Northeast as fuel prices are surging weeks before the midterm elections.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The Energy Department plans to loan 315,000 barrels from the 1 million barrel Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, according to a statement Wednesday. Deliveries are scheduled to be completed by Nov. 13.
"This is a temporary measure to solve a temporary supply disruption," Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in the statement.
The average price of diesel, which has hit record highs during the Iran war, is about $6.32 a gallon, according to AAA. About 4% of the nation's households use heating oil, including in Maine, New Hampshire and Alaska — all of which are politically competitive.
The diesel fuel reserve, housed in commercial storage facilities across the Northeast, was used in the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy in 2012 to provide fuel for emergency responders in New York and New Jersey, as well as in the wake of snowstorms that same year.
Created under former President Bill Clinton, the reserve is designed to provide the Northeast 10 days of supply, which is roughly the time it takes for ships to bring additional heating oil from the Gulf of Mexico to New York Harbor, according to the Energy Department.
The Trump administration last year proposed selling the reserve, which the Energy Department estimated would generate $100 million.
Wright said in the statement that the governors of New York and New England should approve a proposed pipeline that the Trump administration is pushing to build to bring more natural gas to the region.

"This is a temporary measure to solve a temporary supply disruption," Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in the statement.

The average price of diesel, which has hit record highs during the Iran war, is about $6.32 a gallon, according to AAA. About 4% of the nation's households use heating oil, including in Maine, New Hampshire and Alaska — all of which are politically competitive.

The diesel fuel reserve, housed in commercial storage facilities across the Northeast, was used in the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy in 2012 to provide fuel for emergency responders in New York and New Jersey, as well as in the wake of snowstorms that same year.

Created under former President Bill Clinton, the reserve is designed to provide the Northeast 10 days of supply, which is roughly the time it takes for ships to bring additional heating oil from the Gulf of Mexico to New York Harbor, according to the Energy Department.

The Trump administration last year proposed selling the reserve, which the Energy Department estimated would generate $100 million.

Wright said in the statement that the governors of New York and New England should approve a proposed pipeline that the Trump administration is pushing to build to bring more natural gas to the region.

item.title: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
2026-10-22
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-to-publicly-file-for-ipo-as-early-as-friday-sources-say-135343841.html
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) is set to publicly file its S-1 investor prospectus as soon as Friday, according to three people familiar with the artificial intelligence firm's plans. The move would mark a crucial next step for what could be the biggest IPO in history.
The much-anticipated public debut, expected to surpass SpaceX's (SPCX) June IPO, is widely viewed as a crucial test of investor appetite for the artificial intelligence boom, as investors have become more concerned about the industry's massive spending.
Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft IPO registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in June. Under SEC rules, companies using the confidential process must make their registration materials available 15 calendar days before the start of their formal investor roadshow.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment on the timing of its S-1.
A public filing would clear a key procedural hurdle toward a potential November listing, though the timing of the offering remains subject to market conditions and other factors. Crucially, it would also give regular investors their first look at the financial details and risks around one of the AI industry's fastest-growing companies.
Anthropic is spending billions on AI infrastructure to train and run its suite of Claude models. That includes working with Google (GOOG, GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN), as well as renting out graphics processor unit (GPU) capacity from SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center.
The company pulled in $16.3 billion in revenue over the first six months of 2026 and reported a net loss of over $80 billion, according to a Tuesday Wall Street Journal report. Wall Street is anticipating that the company could raise as much as $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters previously reported.
Last week, Anthropic told investors at its San Francisco office that its revenue climbed to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up from $11.5 billion in the second quarter, according to the Financial Times, noting that the company is also profitable on an adjusted basis.
The colossal offering comes as this year's banner IPO market is becoming more challenging. Earlier this week, shares of South Korean data center provider Elice plummeted a staggering 32% during its first trading day after raising $151 million. Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid abruptly shelved plans for a public listing earlier this month after investors balked at its proposed valuation, while several other companies have postponed plans to go public, citing market conditions.

item.title: Kalshi could be headed for Supreme Court showdown, CEO says
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
Kalshi could be headed for Supreme Court showdown, CEO says
2026-10-22
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/options/articles/kalshi-could-headed-supreme-court-152217818.html
DUBLIN, Oct 21 (Reuters) - A legal clash between prediction markets and US states over who should regulate the industry could eventually end up at the Supreme Court, Tarek Mansour, the co-founder of Kalshi, told Reuters.
"I think the process will play out the way it's going to play out," Mansour, who is chief executive of the platform, said on the Reuters Econ World podcast.
Dozens of states have taken legal action over sports-related trades on Kalshi, a prediction markets platform that offers users yes-or-no bets on everything from which political party will control Congress after next month's midterms to who will win the current season of "Dancing with the Stars."
The states say prediction markets like Kalshi are subject to state gambling laws and gambling taxes. Kalshi argues that its wagers aren't gambling and should be exempt from state supervision. The company says sports contracts traded on its platform are a type of financial derivative and are subject to federal regulation under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).
Federal appeals courts have so far split, with Kalshi on the losing end of some recent cases. But the platform secured a big appeals court victory in the action brought against it by New Jersey, which has asked for a Supreme Court review.
Mansour declined to comment on Kalshi's odds of winning if the Supreme Court agrees to take up the case, but said the company was very confident in its legal position.
"Frankly, the statute and the structure is very, very clear and, you know, whether people think a sports game is a game, this commodities exchange act gave the CFTC the authority to decide what to do with the game, and to regulate it the way it sees fit, and that's what it's doing."
At stake is the future of a booming industry. The prediction market has surged in recent years with an explosion in sports betting, helping drive Kalshi's valuation to around $40 billion in a new funding round, according to people familiar with the matter.
Mansour said sports currently accounts for close to 65% of its revenue, compared to around 95% nine months ago.
A Supreme Court victory for Kalshi could cement its position as a leader in prediction markets and boost its push to become a one-stop trading platform for a wide array of asset classes competing with traditional exchange heavyweights, like CME Group and Intercontinental Exchange, the parent of the New York Stock Exchange. A defeat would leave the company vulnerable to states that want to maintain tight control over gaming and could crimp its profits from sports wagers.
(Reporting by Carmel Crimmins; Editing by Daniel Wallis)

item.title: A New Approach for AI Investing
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
A New Approach for AI Investing
2026-10-21
Por Texto propio
A New Approach for AI Investing
morganstanley.com
Key Takeaways
- AI earnings momentum is broadening. Enablers remain strong, while adopters are beginning to see a meaningful improvement in fundamentals.
- The AI trade is shifting toward select enablers as well as adopters whose improving fundamentals may not be fully reflected in expectations.
- AI’s potential productivity impact and rapidly improving LLM capabilities could give adopters a larger role than they played in any previous technology cycles, a benefit the market may be underestimating.
- Companies addressing data center bottlenecks—energy supply, labor and regulation—could benefit as demand for compute rises.
- The broad-reaching impacts of artificial intelligence are becoming more visible every day. So are the effects on the earnings of companies developing or adopting the technology, as well as those building the infrastructure needed to support it.
Morgan Stanley Research recently mapped the ~3,600 stocks under our global coverage to better understand how AI exposure is affecting companies across sectors.
Our analysis suggests that investing in the AI theme is transitioning to a new approach: Investors should continue owning select enablers with durable earnings while increasingly adding adopters whose improving fundamentals aren’t fully reflected in expectations. Another opportunity lies with companies addressing key bottlenecks in data center development.
What’s Different in This New Phase
Technology enablers—including semiconductor, infrastructure and software companies—have traditionally outperformed during computing cycles as investors view them as the primary providers of the technology stack.
Adopters, or companies that leverage new technologies to drive productivity gains and revenue growth, typically benefit after enablers.
In this new phase, however, our research suggests that the spread of AI across industries could drive greater outperformance among adopters than in previous technology cycles, and that the market may still be underestimating how much value AI can create for them. The exponential growth of large language model capabilities and AI’s potential impact on productivity suggest a broader and more meaningful opportunity for value creation.
Investing in the AI theme is evolving: Investors should continue owning select enablers with durable earnings while increasingly adding adopters whose improving fundamentals aren’t fully reflected in expectations.
At the same time, demand for computing capacity is likely to significantly exceed supply for years to come. Three major bottlenecks are constraining the pace of data center development: energy supply that isn’t keeping up with demand, labor constraints and regulatory hurdles.
As a result, we expect market leadership over the next six to 12 months to be concentrated among power companies that can address data center bottlenecks; select semiconductor and infrastructure companies; and early software enablers and AI adopters that are already translating the technology into productivity and revenue benefits. Late-stage software enablers and service companies are likely to benefit later in the cycle.
What the Mapping of 3,600 Stocks Shows
Earnings estimates still don’t reflect long-term benefits of AI adoption: Consensus estimates are beginning to include benefits of AI adoption, but primarily in the near term. However, we think AI-driven productivity gains for adopters could prove more durable than the market expects, creating potential upside to longer-term.
AI momentum is broadening: The next phase of AI leadership is more likely to broaden rather than completely rotate. Enablers continue to show the strongest earnings momentum, but adopters are also seeing a meaningful inflection.
Valuation divergence is improving adopters’ Risk/Reward: The median forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) for adopters has fallen to 18, b

item.title: Meta's Muse AI agent hits 10.9 million downloads as ChatGPT slides 25%
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Meta's Muse AI agent hits 10.9 million downloads as ChatGPT slides 25%
2026-10-21
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/metas-muse-ai-agent-hits-109-million-downloads-as-chatgpt-slides-25-153532560.html
If the excitement around Meta's (META) new Muse AI agent is slowing down, you certainly don't see it in the download numbers Wall Street is tracking like a hawk.
Meta's Muse has amassed 10.9 million downloads since its launch on Sept. 8, according to newly released data from Sensor Tower. Muse has received more than 10.2 million downloads from the US alone.
In contrast, US downloads for OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) ChatGPT in the past 30 days have declined by 25% over the prior 30-day period.
Sensor Tower estimated that Muse reached 2.5 million daily active users (DAUs) for the first time on Oct. 16, as DAUs increased 15% week over week for the past seven days.
The momentum is likely welcome news to Wall Street, which has come out with aggressive growth assumptions for Muse since its release.
Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black sees Muse reaching up to 8% of Meta's revenue by 2030, which nets out to roughly $36 billion in sales for the product. On the lower end of the prediction scale, Black sees Muse pulling in sales of $2.4 billion by 2030.
"In our view, Meta found a clear gap amongst current AI-agentic offerings — at the intersection of mobile app-based ecosystem, with a consumer-oriented UI which is seamless to use, the ability to complete transactions autonomously, free-to-use for the most part, and always-on feature within its own virtual machine — that makes it the service virtually unique in today's market," Black said.
Meta is slated to report earnings after the close of trading on Wednesday.

item.title: Netflix has 2 problems behind the stock slide — and they aren't YouTube, co-CEO Ted Sarandos says
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Netflix has 2 problems behind the stock slide — and they aren't YouTube, co-CEO Ted Sarandos says
2026-10-21
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/netflix-has-2-problems-behind-the-stock-slide--and-they-arent-youtube-co-ceo-ted-sarandos-says-121935914.html
And they can't be fixed immediately by laying off 6% of the workforce and, surprisingly, by pushing out Bela Bajaria as chief content officer in favor of former Disney (DIS) exec Peter Rice, as seen this week.
In the end, a Netflix growth reboot will hinge on a steady pipeline of fresh creative talent and more content home runs.
"Most importantly, Rob, Peter Rice understands talent relations, and in a competitive market, creative talent have choices of where they want to work, and we want Netflix to always be the place that they love to do the best work of their life. Peter is the exact right person to lead those efforts in the U.S. and around the world," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said on the company's earnings call late Tuesday.
"The U.S. is also working," he continued. "It's just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we'd like. We had some really solid doubles and triples this year. But the other territories count on some of those titles being home runs so that they'll travel around the world."
Netflix delivered a mixed third quarter earnings report amid those doubles and triples on the content front, with earnings of $0.87 per share, beating Wall Street estimates of $0.82.
Revenue of $12.87 billion came in line with analysts' expectations.
For the fourth quarter, Netflix forecast revenue of $13.44 billion, below expectations of $13.57 billion.
The company also cut its full-year advertising revenue outlook to about $2.7 billion from $3 billion previously.
Netflix stock fell 6% in premarket trading. The stock had been down 26% this year ahead of the earnings release.
"2026 has been more of a transitional year than we envisioned. While the latest Ads miss is frustrating, we find comfort in Membership retention that is still healthy and corrective actions within content that can drive a potential re-acceleration in 2027E and into 2028E (which we are not modeling today)," KeyBanc Justin Patterson said.

item.title: The era of 'tokenmaxxing' is over — and investors shouldn't take unlimited AI demand for granted
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
The era of 'tokenmaxxing' is over — and investors shouldn't take unlimited AI demand for granted
2026-10-21
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-era-of-tokenmaxxing-is-over--and-investors-shouldnt-take-unlimited-ai-demand-for-granted-100000961.html
The era of tokenmaxxing is officially over. That's because the demand for computing capacity isn't actually unlimited, as AI boosters once touted.
Instead, compute appears to be highly price-sensitive, as buyers facing higher prices and lower returns cut back on usage or pivot to cheap open-source alternatives.
That's the key finding in a new blog post by Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk: don't take AI demand for granted.
(Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
Ultimately, the key metric that will define the AI build-out isn't physical capacity or power, Sløk said, but the price users are willing to pay for the compute being built. And token spending has sharply decreased.
The slowdown in token spending among corporations suggests that the lavish appetite for compute only exists at the right price — when it is effectively free.
An analysis of declining returns on invested capital for the five largest hyperscalers suggests invested capital grows faster than the earnings it generates. That mismatch gets at the heart of the AI bull case and gives investors questions to ask and numbers to watch for as we get deeper into Big Tech earnings.
Companies are willing to pay a high price for compute, he said, if they are able to boost revenues, squeeze out better profit margins, or cut costs. But such results at a meaningful scale aren't showing up yet.
So far, he said, the AI payoff has been slow to materialize. That suggests more companies are reluctant to dedicate resources to pay for AI services. Those returns may actually emerge. But the uncertainty comes at a price.
Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban.

item.title: United Airlines CEO: 'We should have a national wealth tax'
item.author: Molly Moorhead
item.description:
United Airlines CEO: 'We should have a national wealth tax'
2026-10-21
Por Molly Moorhead
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/united-airlines-ceo-we-should-have-a-national-wealth-tax-092341353.html
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby gave a wide-ranging, often provocative interview to the New York Times, defending fees for aisle and window seats and countering the rise in airfares by asserting "it's expensive to fly airplanes."
"There are customers that pay more that get more," Kirby, 59, said in the interview that ran Oct. 18.
But he struck a decidedly more populist note on the topic of wealth inequality — which he brought up when the Times asked him about waning trust in CEOs and his responsibility in dispelling it. Here's his full answer:
"Wealth inequality has become a danger to our society, and we need to address that," he said. "We should have a national wealth tax — it won't work by state because people will just move. And I think we should have inheritance taxes that get close to 100% at some level. I would pay them."
United Airlines stock rose 0.3% before the bell on Tuesday.
Kirby is not the first or only business titan to call for bigger taxes on the wealthiest Americans. Luminaries like Warren Buffett, Bill Gates, and George Soros have long advocated for increasing the tax burden at their rarefied wealth levels.
Read more: How much does a millionaire actually owe the IRS on tax day?
"We've updated our tax system before to keep up with changing times, and we need to do it again, starting with raising taxes on people like me," Gates wrote on his blog in 2020.
Marc Benioff, CEO of Salesforce (CRM), wrote in 2019 that "increasing taxes on high-income individuals like myself would help generate the trillions of dollars that we desperately need to improve education and healthcare and fight climate change."
Joe Biden was president, and Democrats in Congress were gearing up to pass legislation to tax unrealized gains on individuals with a net worth of at least $1 billion or annual income of $100 million for three consecutive years. Of course, that never happened, and after President Trump was reelected, Republicans in Congress passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which included provisions that made lower marginal tax rates for high incomes permanent, along with other provisions benefiting wealthy Americans.
Read more: 10 ways the One Big Beautiful Bill Act affects student loans and financial aid
As for the inheritance taxes Kirby said he favors, there is no federal tax on individual beneficiaries of inherited assets. A few states impose a state inheritance tax.
There is a federal estate tax, but the exemption is so large — $15 million per person — that few people ever pay it. Only 0.2% of estates are large enough to be subject to the tax, and even then the tax applies only to the amount that exceeds the exemption threshold.
Molly Moorhead is economics editor for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Great Scott! The AI-fueled data center build-out could double next year: Chart of the Day
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Great Scott! The AI-fueled data center build-out could double next year: Chart of the Day
2026-10-21
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/great-scott-the-ai-fueled-data-center-build-out-could-double-next-year-chart-of-the-day-100000440.html
Doc Brown needed 1.21 gigawatts to send a DeLorean through time in the 1985 movie "Back to the Future." The data-center industry could add about 42 times that next year.
Welcome to the Doc Brown Index.
Research firm SemiAnalysis expects annual additions to data center IT capacity outside China to more than double next year, to about 51 gigawatts from 25 gigawatts this year.
In movie units, that's about 21 Doc Browns ballooning to 42. These are additions in a single year, not the whole fleet or the electricity it uses. By SemiAnalysis's count, that one year would roughly match the world's entire data center build-out through 2024.
About three-quarters of next year's projected additions come from projects already operational or under construction. The rest are still planned. SemiAnalysis points to more than 24 gigawatts across 40 campuses in advanced construction for expected delivery next year.
Not everyone buys it. At the All-In Summit in September, Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner called SemiAnalysis's forecast at the time, 43 gigawatts, too aggressive and guessed the industry would stand up closer to 25 gigawatts. That's only about 21 Doc Browns — no faster than this year.
How do you build that much, that quickly? Increasingly, in pieces.
Suppliers now build electrical rooms and cooling systems in factories while crews prepare the site. SemiAnalysis calls the results Lego data centers, with bricks that can weigh 50,000 pounds.
Amazon (AMZN) is rolling out its own modular design at large scale, and Meta Platforms (META) has put up tent-like halls to enclose buildings faster, according to SemiAnalysis.
A SemiAnalysis model of a 50-megawatt AI data hall puts conventional construction at 22 months and a fully modular approach at 14, excluding permitting. The biggest saving comes from electrical and mechanical installation. For the owner of the chips inside, SemiAnalysis values that eight-month head start at about $200 million.
That shift puts suppliers in the race alongside chipmakers such as Nvidia (NVDA). SemiAnalysis estimates content per megawatt for Vertiv (VRT) roughly doubles, to as much as $7 million, when it sells the full modular stack. Contractors Comfort Systems USA (FIX) and Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) assemble modules too.
But a finished building still needs power.
Microsoft (MSFT) confirmed Monday that it pulled out of a lease at a planned 50-megawatt Nscale data center outside London — the same size as the SemiAnalysis model — after grid officials said power might not arrive until the 2030s. Microsoft said the decision involved a single site and that its broader partnership with Nscale continues.

Suppliers now build electrical rooms and cooling systems in factories while crews prepare the site. SemiAnalysis calls the results Lego data centers, with bricks that can weigh 50,000 pounds.
Amazon (AMZN) is rolling out its own modular design at large scale, and Meta Platforms (META) has put up tent-like halls to enclose buildings faster, according to SemiAnalysis.
A SemiAnalysis model of a 50-megawatt AI data hall puts conventional construction at 22 months and a fully modular approach at 14, excluding permitting. The biggest saving comes from electrical and mechanical installation. For the owner of the chips inside, SemiAnalysis values that eight-month head start at about $200 million.
That shift puts suppliers in the race alongside chipmakers such as Nvidia (NVDA). SemiAnalysis estimates content per megawatt for Vertiv (VRT) roughly doubles, to as much as $7 million, when it sells the full modular stack. Contractors Comfort Systems USA (FIX) and Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) assemble modules too.
But a finished building still needs power.
Microsoft (MSFT) confirmed Monday that it pulled out of a lease at a planned 50-megawatt Nscale data center outside London — the same size as the SemiAnalysis model — after grid officials said power might not arrive until the 2030s. Microsoft said the decision involved a single site and that its broader partnership with Nscale continues.

item.title: Walmart goes on offense to win the subscription space, offering new bundle for one price
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Walmart goes on offense to win the subscription space, offering new bundle for one price
2026-10-21
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/walmart-goes-on-offense-to-win-the-subscription-space-offering-new-bundle-for-one-price-100000929.html
As many Americans say they're strapped by subscription fatigue, Walmart is looking to make its offerings more enticing by combining Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus for $120 a year, plus tax.
The all-in-one offering announced Tuesday is only available annually, with no monthly option or trial. If you were to purchase each offer separately, Walmart+ costs $98 plus tax per year, or $12.95 plus tax per month, and its wholesale membership, Sam's Club Plus, costs $120 a year. A basic club membership runs $60.
Walmart (WMT) posted its slowest US same-store sales growth last quarter since Q4 of 2020, at 2.6%. Now the retailer is hoping it can recapture share it may have lost to others like Target (TGT), Amazon (AMZN), Costco (COST), and BJ's (BJ).
"We're giving people a reason to expect more from their memberships … we're raising expectations for what a membership can deliver: more money in their pockets and more time to call their own," Walmart CEO John Furner said in a release.
Here's how Walmart's subscription bundle compares with competitors:
Target Circle 360 is $4.99 per month or $49 per year. Amazon Prime costs $140 a year.
A standard Costco membership runs $65 a year, whereas the executive membership costs $130. For a standard BJ's membership, it's $60 per year or $120 for BJ's Club+.
The membership model is a sizeable opportunity for Walmart, per Bank of America analyst Christopher Nardone, who said in a recent note, "Walmart+ members spend approximately 4x more compared to non-members."
He added that advertising, marketplace growth, and global membership remain healthy and reaffirmed confidence "that the broader flywheel to improve longer-term profitability remains intact. "
He added, "These businesses give Walmart an advantage to navigate the challenging pricing and supply chain environment in the near term, but longer-term continued execution across these businesses should help improve longer-term profitability versus today's levels."
Deutsche Bank analyst Krisztina Katai recently upgraded the stock to a Buy rating from Neutral, citing that "the current inflationary environment should reinforce Walmart's value proposition and support accelerated share gains."
All employees will now get both memberships to Walmart and Sam's Club as part of their benefits. Last week, the company announced plans to cover over 250 medications, including insulin and inhalers for $0 and GLP-1s for diabetes.
Brooke DiPalma is a reporter for Yahoo Finance. Follow her on X at @BrookeDiPalma or email her at bdipalma@yahoofinance.com.

item.title: Meta and Google are about to have a consumer AI showdown
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Meta and Google are about to have a consumer AI showdown
2026-10-21
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/meta-and-google-are-about-to-have-a-consumer-ai-showdown-100000834.html
The race to put out a widely adopted and highly competent digital assistant is a fight to control the next popular tech platform. It just so happens that the companies poised for a heated confrontation over AI agents are also the two dominant digital advertising firms.
Meta (META), which reports quarterly results Tuesday, and Google (GOOG) are headed for an AI showdown.
Last month Meta's Muse burst onto the scene, delivering the first popular AI agent for normies, and just cracked a download milestone. Muse's early success, in both downloads and praise, previewed a world where more people rely on their digital helpers to get work done and manage their daily routines.
More cautious tech users might wait for the first wave of early adopters to find the bugs and iron out the kinks. The trust that goes with safeguarding emails, calendars, and wallets hasn't historically been Meta's purview. Better to hold out for whatever consumer-focused agent the iPhone maker or the Gmail company has in store.
First-mover status has won Meta public goodwill and an upward jolt in its stock price. Still, that hasn't made the threat from its advertising rival any less potent.
Several analysts have said that Google's future agent offering is a key risk facing Meta. Being first is often good enough in the tech world. But what comes second can be better — or more trusted. And in the uncharted territory of new AI services, early, tech-oriented users are likely to be different from the masses of people who enter the market later on.
"Google remains well positioned to lead in the AI era supported by proprietary models, custom silicon & broad product distribution," wrote Bank of America analysts led by Justin Post in a note earlier this week. He added that a competitive agent and broader Gemini 4 launch could be catalysts for the search giant.
Another point of tension between Meta and Google is how their legacy businesses can help or hurt their AI ambitions.
Google and Meta are the top dogs in the digital advertising market. They account for more than half of global ad revenue. But one of the crucial ideas behind AI agents is moving away from a screen-phone-app interface. Mobile apps prospered because they allowed for an easier, more intuitive form of computing. AI agents, taken to the extreme, promise to do away with computing altogether, or at least in the way we are used to.

item.title: Trump announces $8 billion for farmers to offset soaring diesel costs
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Trump announces $8 billion for farmers to offset soaring diesel costs
2026-10-21
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/trump-announces-8-billion-for-farmers-to-offset-soaring-diesel-costs-111330890.html
President Trump announced an $8 billion aid package on Monday to help US farmers pay for diesel this harvest season.
The relief program, announced at a campaign rally in Kansas and on social media, aims to bring down fuel costs for Americans ahead of next month's midterm elections.
"Tonight, I am also pleased to announce that the Department of Agriculture will be launching a new 'Harvest Fuel Relief Program,' providing our Farmers with 8 BILLION DOLLARS in support to offset Diesel costs during this Harvest Season," Trump's account posted on Truth Social (DJT).
"When Republicans win, we will pass even more funding for our Great Farmers, and Fuel prices will come tumbling down as soon as the Iran War is over, which will happen very quickly!" he added.
The Harvest Fuel Relief Program will be administered by the US Department of Agriculture. Trump credited Republican Sen. Roger Marshall of Kansas with helping advance the initiative.
The White House move comes as nearly every corner of the economy, including farming and transportation, grapples with soaring energy input costs.
Diesel prices on Tuesday hovered near a national average of about $6.32 per gallon after hitting a record high in September, driven by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, as well as constrained global refining capacity.
Read more: The US economy is facing 2 hot wars heating up at a bad time for the White House
The aid program won't directly lower fuel costs but will provide one-time payments through the USDA's Farm Service Agency (FSA) to help farmers offset these expenses.
Earlier this month, the Trump administration moved to lift restrictions on red-dyed diesel, a tax-exempt fuel typically reserved for tractors and farm gear. The measure allows its use in standard highway vehicles.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: US housing market likely to stay bleak, Goldman Sachs warns
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
US housing market likely to stay bleak, Goldman Sachs warns
2026-10-21
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/us-housing-market-likely-to-stay-bleak-goldman-sachs-warns-133222926.html
US housing market conditions are unlikely to change much just because the calendar turns from 2026 to 2027, Goldman Sachs warned.
Elevated mortgage rates will keep homeownership out of reach for many Americans and, in turn, weigh on the US economy.
"In 2027, we expect the headwind from affordability — reignited by the recent rebound in mortgage rates — to increasingly dominate, weighing further on activity," Goldman Sachs analyst Ronnie Walker said. "Sustained higher mortgage rates will continue to have their most pronounced impact on housing turnover, and the recent run-up in rates is likely to push existing home sales lower in the coming months. More than 95% of mortgage borrowers have interest rates below current market rates, and 65% have rates 2 percentage points below market rates, strongly disincentivizing them from moving."
Read more: How to get the lowest mortgage rates right now
Walker estimated existing home sales of just 3.9 million in 2027, 26% below 2019 levels and slightly shy of his 4 million estimate for 2026.
"We expect housing demand to remain tepid," Walker added.
The housing affordability crisis is likely to continue to weigh on young people looking to buy a home.
About 9 in 10 adults younger than 40 say it's harder for young adults today to buy a home than it was for their parents' generation, according to a recent Pew Research Center survey.
Since 2019, home prices in the US have risen faster than young adults' incomes, according to the Pew Research data.
Between 2019 and 2024, the inflation-adjusted median home value rose 30%, Pew noted, while the inflation-adjusted median household income for households headed by those under 40 rose only 9%.
At this point, housing experts think young people need to get more creative in the home-buying process if they ever want a piece of the American dream.
"Well, one thing that's going on within the housing market is you're seeing — and this is also with the 21st Century housing bill that passed just several months ago — is you're going into blighted areas and investing in the rehabilitation of those homes. And that's actually a much cheaper way of owning a home than otherwise," Meredith Whitney, CEO of Meredith Whitney Advisory Group, said on Sozzi Unleashed.
"Detroit's the perfect example of this," she added, "where you had an economic revival with blighted areas, with run-down areas and investment in those areas. You can get a home for a massive discount to what you would have in the more established areas. And these areas are getting also economic investment from corporations. And you're seeing real revival."

item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
GM beats on Q3 results, tightens profit outlook, unveils new $20 billion buyback

item.title: Anthropic May Spend $750 Billion on Computing Costs, Report Says
item.author: David Morris
item.description:
Anthropic May Spend $750 Billion on Computing Costs, Report Says
2026-10-21
Por David Morris
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/anthropic-may-spend-750-billion-200421561.html
(Bloomberg) -- Anthropic PBC could spend $750 billion on additional computing power in the coming years, according to a Wall Street Journal report, as the company prepares for an initial public offering.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The artificial intelligence firm had a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, the media outlet reported, citing a draft IPO prospectus. That compares to a net loss of $13 billion in the corresponding period a year ago, WSJ said.
The overwhelming majority of the net loss in the first half of this year, $72 billion, resulted from accounting charges linked to changes in the value of convertible notes and other instruments Anthropic has issued, according to the report.
Anthropic, one of the leading AI developers, is expected to publicly file paperwork for a Wall Street debut in the coming weeks, setting it up for what could be one of the largest IPOs ever. The listing will help the company raise additional capital to support its investments in chips, data centers and talent to build new and better AI models.
The company behind Claude spent close to $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the six months ended June 30, versus $2.3 billion in the same period in 2025, according to the Journal. Anthropic deployed more funds to secure computing power in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025, when it spent $7.3 billion.
The prospectus shows Anthropic's extensive web of computing power agreements — totaling around $450 billion in the next seven to 10 years — the majority of which can't be canceled, according to the Journal. The company plans to spend $111 billion on contracts with Alphabet Inc.'s Google Cloud, $110 billion with Amazon.com Inc.'s Amazon Web Services and $31 billion with Microsoft Corp.
Anthropic's prospectus flags the risk of damages caused by AI, including the potential for models to show "self-preserving" qualities to avoid being turned off, and responses that resemble "blackmail" to keep humans from preventing them from operating, the report shows. Anthropic could also face the risk of political resistance to building data centers in the US, where most of its capacity is, according to the Journal.
The company told investors it had achieved profitability in the third quarter on an adjusted basis, Bloomberg News has reported. Anthropic is generating positive free cash flow, had gross margin of 85% and an over 11% positive adjusted operating margin as of the third quarter, people familiar with the matter have said.

item.title: Netflix stock sinks after announcing Q3 earnings, Q4 revenue forecast falls short of estimates
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Netflix stock sinks after announcing Q3 earnings, Q4 revenue forecast falls short of estimates
2026-10-21
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/netflix-stock-sinks-after-announcing-q3-earnings-q4-revenue-forecast-falls-short-of-estimates-204545261.html
Netflix (NFLX) stock fell 6% in premarket trading on Wednesday as the streaming giant's Q4 revenue outlook came in below Wall Street estimates, signaling slower growth.
The company posted revenue of $12.87 billion in its fiscal third quarter, in line with analyst estimates. Earnings per share came in at $0.87, topping estimates of $0.82.
Fourth-quarter outlook for the company's top line, though, came in at $13.44 billion, short of the consensus analyst estimate of $13.51 billion.
Netflix also cut its 2026 ad revenue guidance from $3 billion to $2.7 billion due to a slower-than-expected rollout of certain ad product capabilities.
Wall Street has been laser-focused on engagement, which management argued was healthy given the response to this year's price increases.
When it comes to the US, "our engagement is solid, and it will allow us to continue to grow as we have for the last several years," Greg Peters, co-CEO of Netflix, said during the earnings call.
"But we know that we can do better…It's our goal to go from very good to great," he added.
Wall Street analysts were looking for signs on whether slowing engagement would bleed into the revenue growth numbers.
"That is exactly what we are seeing with the 4Q growth outlook," Geetha Ranganathan, senior media analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, told Yahoo Finance after the results were released.
"This kind of speaks to a slowing growth algorithm, which kind of spells trouble for the company without a doubt," she added.
The results follow the streaming giant's job-cutting plan and a leadership shake-up announced last week amid slowing viewer engagement.
Last week, former Disney executive Peter Rice was named Netflix's next chief content officer. Rice replaces Bela Bajaria, who worked at the streamer for nearly a decade and served as CCO since 2023.
Also last week, Netflix said it would cut 6% of its workforce, or about 1,000 employees, marking the company's largest reduction of employees since 2022.
The move comes as the company seeks to reinvigorate viewership growth and strengthen its content amid growing competition and short-form viewing habits.
Audiences have increasingly moved away from traditional television sets toward mobile devices, noted Piper Sandler director and senior research analyst Tom Champion in a recent interview.

item.title: Mejor entorno de confianza
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Mejor entorno de confianza
2026-10-20
Por Texto propio
¿Mejor entorno de confianza?
Pablo Lucio Paredes
Columna publicada en diario El Universo, sábado 12 de Septiembre de 2026.
Visita de Marco Rubio
Conocemos la posición global de EEUU con tres ejes claves. Uno, controlar el mercado del petróleo y tierras raras. Dos, evitar la expansión china en particular en Latinoamérica. Tres, frenar la explosión del fentanilo, grave problema en la sociedad americana. ¿Dónde entramos nosotros? Quizás en los tres, pero con una compleja duda ¿qué damos a cambio? ¿cómo nos posicionamos en este juego? Ojalá no sea lo que sucede en Venezuela y Bolivia donde la relación parece ir con graves negociados e intereses particulares.
Tema: la confianza.
Estemos conscientes que el desarrollo se sustenta en varios factores, unos más estrictamente económicos o legales, otros institucionales. ¿Qué es esto último? Una definición de la RAE “Una costumbre, regla o pauta social muy arraigada”. Efectivamente son los mecanismos explícitos o implícitos alrededor de los cuales funciona una sociedad. Uno de ellos, clave, es la confianza que se expresa así: “expectativa sobre la conducta futura (positiva) de los demás y (pre)condición necesaria para la cooperación humana y la vida en sociedad”. Esto se aplica a diversos ámbitos y preguntémonos cómo estamos en el país…
(Des)confianza entre personas.
Muchos trabajos muestran que no confiamos, más allá del círculo familiar muy cercano. Más bien “actuamos con viveza criolla” (mal) antes que los demás se aprovechen de nosotros. Ejemplo sencillo, el tráfico: ¿confiamos en que los demás actuarán correctamente? ¿un peatón en un paso zebra, confía que los vehículos le dejarán pasar? Y más ampliamente ¿creemos que la mayor parte de gente actuará honestamente en la mayor parte de casos, o corrupción y viveza siguen campantes?
(Des)confianza institucional.
¿Creemos que las leyes se aplican de manera justa para todos? En particular: ¿creemos que la justicia cumple su rol y no favorece al que es capaz de sobornar a los jueces? Y más ampliamente: ¿estamos o no, viendo cómo se utilizan la justicia y la política para perseguir a los adversarios (que obviamente merecen ser sancionados si han delinquido) pero jamás a los propios? Opiniones negativas sobre el pasado y desgraciadamente igual ahora.
(Des)confianza económica.
Pregunta sencilla: si usted quiere ampliar su negocio invirtiendo o contratando más gente ¿su primera reacción es “hay los riesgos normales de cualquier negocio, pero me lanzo” o piensa dos veces y se frena porque “no confía en el entorno del país que es demasiado riesgoso”? Probablemente lo segundo. Claro, porque hay todo el tema de violencia desde las vacunas hasta los riesgos a la vida misma,
constantes limitaciones a la libertad y enorme irrespeto a los contratos. ¿En algo hemos mejorado? Sí en lo muy macro, así lo dice el excelente Índice de Incertidumbre de la USFQ: “aumentó en el segundo semestre 2025 e inicios 2026 por la eliminación del subsidio al
diésel, protestas y bloqueos, referéndum de noviembre, escalada de tensiones con Colombia, y desde febrero ha mejorado en un contexto de mayor estabilidad macroeconómica y retorno a los mercados internacionales” … Pero riesgos y desconfianza siguen ahí presentes frenando la calidad de vida, aumentando los costos de funcionamiento de la sociedad y (de)construyendo su estructura.

¿Mejor entorno de confianza?
Pablo Lucio Paredes
Columna publicada en diario El Universo, sábado 12 de Septiembre de 2026.
Visita de Marco Rubio
Conocemos la posición global de EEUU con tres ejes claves. Uno, controlar el mercado del petróleo y tierras raras. Dos, evitar la expansión china en particular en Latinoamérica. Tres, frenar la explosión del fentanilo, grave problema en la sociedad americana. ¿Dónde entramos nosotros? Quizás en los tres, pero con una compleja duda ¿qué damos a cambio? ¿cómo nos posicionamos en este juego? Ojalá no sea lo que sucede en Venezuela y Bolivia donde la relación parece ir con graves negociados e intereses particulares.
Tema: la confianza.
Estemos conscientes que el desarrollo se sustenta en varios factores, unos más estrictamente económicos o legales, otros institucionales. ¿Qué es esto último? Una definición de la RAE “Una costumbre, regla o pauta social muy arraigada”. Efectivamente son los mecanismos explícitos o implícitos alrededor de los cuales funciona una sociedad. Uno de ellos, clave, es la confianza que se expresa así: “expectativa sobre la conducta futura (positiva) de los demás y (pre)condición necesaria para la cooperación humana y la vida en sociedad”. Esto se aplica a diversos ámbitos y preguntémonos cómo estamos en el país…
(Des)confianza entre personas.

Ejemplo sencillo, el tráfico: ¿confiamos en que los demás actuarán correctamente? ¿un peatón en un paso zebra, confía que los vehículos le dejarán pasar? item.title: Amazon blocks agentic AI shopping. But Walmart is betting big that it's worth saying yes.
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Amazon blocks agentic AI shopping. But Walmart is betting big that it's worth saying yes.
2026-10-20
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/amazon-blocks-agentic-ai-shopping-but-walmart-is-betting-big-that-its-worth-saying-yes-100000436.html
Americans like to shop. For a lot of consumers, the act of browsing and filling a digital or physical cart isn't a point of friction but a way of life — just ask Costco influencers.
But in the event that more people delegate their shopping to AI agents, Walmart, and its open embrace of AI partnerships, stands to win.
That's the takeaway in a new note by Bank of America analysts led by Christopher Nardone, published Monday. They cite Walmart's integration with multiple AI ecosystems; the development of the retailer's own shopping assistant named "Sparky"; and its partnerships with other agents, including Meta's Muse, as reasons for Walmart's solid positioning.
Walmart is among the key corporate players partnering with Muse, including Best Buy (BBY) and Ulta (ULTA). These companies are attempting to embrace new modes of digital commerce.
Other retailers have taken an antagonistic approach, choosing to block Muse from interacting with their commercial portals. No doubt there are a number of reasons to block largely untested agents from inserting themselves into your business funnel. But perhaps the most obvious is to prevent another tech platform from becoming a powerful middleman.
Amazon is perhaps the most notable example. The e-commerce giant has blocked Muse from making purchases on its site and prohibits other companies from deploying automated tools to shop.
But Amazon's loss could be Walmart's gain. While Amazon may not be losing much in the way of actual sales — since most people are using AI tools to research rather than to swipe the credit card, so to speak — Walmart is trying to get in early, while habits are still forming.
Still, Walmart's management team, like everyone else, can't say for certain how popular shopping agents will become. And there are other business implications to consider if agents disrupt how people shop. As Nardone noted, if screenless computers are the ones checking out, it remains unclear what happens to the advertising landscape, a business increasingly important to Walmart itself.
Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban.

item.title: US bank stocks' longest losing streak since 2008 clashes with earnings picture
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
US bank stocks' longest losing streak since 2008 clashes with earnings picture
2026-10-20
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/us-bank-stocks-longest-losing-streak-since-2008-clashes-with-earnings-picture-165407807.html
US bank stocks are suffering their longest losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis, despite some of the country's biggest lenders having so far reported another sturdy set of earnings.
Results from the four biggest lenders last week gave fresh evidence that their US consumer and business customers are holding up even in the face of sharply elevated borrowing costs.
JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Bank of America (BAC), Citigroup (C), and Wells Fargo (WFC) collectively set aside $7.6 billion in credit provisions during the quarter, down about 3% from a year earlier. Actual loan losses in the quarter between these same banks fell 5%, while lending grew nearly 10%.
Investors still appear unconvinced. The benchmark KBW Nasdaq Bank Index (^BKX) fell slightly on Monday. It has sold off for the past six consecutive weeks, losing 11% since early September in its longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
The sell-off comes as credit managers worldwide appear increasingly worried about what happens next.
A recent survey of credit portfolio managers at major banks and other global financial institutions found that about 60% expect corporate defaults to rise worldwide over the next 12 months, while 85% anticipate wider spreads on North American junk bonds over the next three months. The figure is sharply higher compared to the survey's second quarter reading of a 40% rise in corporate defaults over the next 12 months and 50% increase in North American junk bonds in the ensuing three months.
Credit portfolio managers "are seeing some risk appetite among investors, but they are also seeing a number of companies, which have so far managed to stay afloat, beginning to reach the end of the line," Som-lok Leung, executive director for the International Association of Credit Portfolio Managers, said in an emailed statement.
Morgan Stanley analysts said in a Monday note to clients that bank credit conditions remain largely "benign," apart from isolated commercial weakness, although executives have sounded generally more cautious on earnings calls so far this month than in the second quarter.
Investor worries center on whether persistently higher interest rates will eventually squeeze borrowers. By the same logic, declining interest rates have "the potential to engineer a bounce" in bank stocks, Bank of America analyst Ebrahim Poonawala wrote Monday.
"Ideally, that occurs on the back of lower energy prices or easing inflation," Poonawala added.

item.title: Worried about a bigger tech stock rout? Find some comfort in this chart.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Worried about a bigger tech stock rout? Find some comfort in this chart.
2026-10-20
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/worried-about-a-bigger-tech-stock-rout-find-some-comfort-in-this-chart-144823122.html
After a brutal stretch for momentum tech stocks the past week, some investors may be warming up to the view that it's time to cash in their chips and head for the hills.
While that is understandable, it's important to keep two things in mind on tech names.
First, major tech stock pullbacks are normal in a bull market, Truist chief markets strategist Keith Lerner pointed out.
Since this bull market began in October 2022, the S&P 500 tech sector has experienced 12 five-day declines of more than 6% and five double-digit pullbacks ranging from 10% to 26%, Lerner said. Semiconductors have experienced five 10-day declines exceeding 15%.
The second point is that the long-term trend on tech is still higher even considering these routs.
Despite these setbacks, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (^SOX) has gained more than 400% during this current bull market. The Technology sector (XLK) has gained 238%, more than double the S&P 500's (^GSPC) 114% return.
All of this is not to downplay what the market has recently digested on tech.
AI chip darling Nvidia (NVDA) shed more than $350 billion in market value last week. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged more than 11%.
Neocloud CoreWeave (CRWV) shed 25% on the week amid rising borrowing costs.
The returning concern: Revenue may not match the billions of dollars companies are investing in AI. How that unfolds for companies using massive amounts of debt to fund their AI investments is a top worry right now.
"The tech love-hate relationship continues. A once-in-a-generation technological advancement offers significant potential, but the wide range of outcomes and the difficulty identifying long-term winners and losers amplify each narrative and data point," Lerner said. "The recent weakness should be viewed in the context of these outsized gains."

item.title: 2 charts show why Wall Street is right to worry about tech stocks
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
2 charts show why Wall Street is right to worry about tech stocks
2026-10-20
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/2-charts-show-why-wall-street-is-right-to-worry-about-tech-stocks-145612923.html
The market is correct in the moment to voice concerns about how the rising cost of capital will impact hyperscalers' financial statements in 2027.
That is because hyperscalers such as Oracle (ORCL) and Google (GOOG, GOOGL) will need fresh debt to fuel their AI infrastructure builds, with free cash flow likely going negative.
JPMorgan strategist Mislav Matejka captured the situation perfectly in the two new charts below.
Hyperscaler free cash flow is forecast to turn negative in 2027, which implies that funding from credit markets is likely to drive more of the AI build-out going forward.
Current consensus estimates for hyperscaler capital expenditures in 2027 are already climbing from levels experts believe are now too low.
Morgan Stanley sees $1.6 trillion in total 2027 capital expenditures among the hyperscalers, up from $978 billion estimated for this year.
"The use cases are accelerating and we see it in the field every day and the capex dollars will be in the trillions with a massive ripple impact across the economy," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives says. "We expect over 1,000 datacenters to be built over the next few years as this next phase of the AI Revolution is set to get built out."
